Adopt the following motion principle for the massive charged test body of [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]]. On any finite segment $z:[a,b]\to O$ in a local potential domain, with $z$ a $C^2$ future-timelike curve and fixed endpoints, the physical trajectories of this idealized model are the stationary points of

$$S[z]=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-g(z',z') }\,d\lambda+q\int_a^b A(z')\,d\lambda,$$

where $\lambda$ is an orientation-preserving curve parameter (use seconds for SI evaluation), $A$ is the prescribed $C^2$ external potential, $F=dA$, $m>0$ is constant rest mass, $q$ is constant charge, and $c$ is the SI conversion constant. With $\lambda=\tau$ in seconds, coordinates in metres and $A$ in tesla metres, $S$ has units joule seconds. The potential and metric are fixed inputs, independent of the particle path. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.

Let $O$ be a potential domain with a $C^2$ metric $g$, a $C^2$ one-form $A$, and $F=dA$. Let $\chi\in C^3(O,\mathbb R)$ and set $A^\chi:=A+d\chi$. For $a<b$, any $C^2$ future-timelike curve segment $z:[a,b]\to O$ parameterized by proper time $\tau$ so $g(z',z')=-c^2$ for $c>0$, constants $m>0$ and $q\in\mathbb R$, and the functional

$$S_A[z]=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-g(z',z') }\,d\tau+q\int_a^b A(z')\,d\tau,$$

the field strength is unchanged, $dA^\chi=dA$, and

$$S_{A^\chi}[z]-S_A[z]=q\bigl(\chi(z(b))-\chi(z(a))\bigr).$$

Thus the difference is constant over every fixed-endpoint variation, so stationarity and the kinetic covector $p:=mU^\flat$ are gauge invariant. If the local covector $\pi_A:=p+qA$ is defined, then $\pi_{A^\chi}=\pi_A+q\,d\chi$. These are local statements on $O$; they assert no global exactness of $F$.

Assume the charged test-body quantities and local potential domain of [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]], the flat-space sign convention of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], and the adopted fixed-endpoint action postulate [[post-rpm-external-charge-action]], and assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure. For a finite $C^2$ future-timelike curve segment $z:[a,b]\to O$ in that domain, where $a<b$ are proper-time endpoints, and the local $C^2$ fixed-endpoint variations of the postulate, choose the orientation-preserving parameter $\lambda=\tau$; the segment is stationary for the adopted action if and only if

$$m\nabla_UU=qF^\sharp(U),\qquad (\nabla_UU)_a=\frac qm F_{ab}U^b.$$

This is a model deduction: it establishes the equation equivalent to stationarity of the postulated functional, not the physical truth of the postulate.

Use the smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian background $(M,g,N)$, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and the distinct chart, observer, congruence, tetrad and worldline meanings of [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. The metric and time orientation are prescribed data, not dynamical variables. Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be order-convex ([[def-interval]]) and let
$f : I \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $I$ ([[def-continuity-real]]) and
differentiable at every point of $I$ that is interior to $I$
([[def-interior-closure-boundary-r]], [[def-derivative]]), with

$$f'(x) = 0 \qquad \text{at every interior point } x \text{ of } I .$$

Then $f$ is constant on $I$: there is a real $k$ with $f(x) = k$ for every
$x \in I$.

Consequently, if $f, g : I \to \mathbb{R}$ are both continuous on $I$ and both
differentiable at every interior point of $I$, with $f'(x) = g'(x)$ at every
interior point $x$, then there is a real $k$ with

$$f(x) \;=\; g(x) + k \qquad \text{for every } x \in I .$$

**Order-convexity of $I$ is essential and is not a convenience.** The
conclusion is false on a domain that falls into separate pieces, since a
function may be constant on each piece with different const

derivations.claim: By [A2] and [F3], stationarity is equivalent to $m\nabla_UU=0$. Since $m>0$ and the metric matrix is constant, [F1] gives $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\eta^{ad}(\partial_b\eta_{dc}+\partial_c\eta_{db}-\partial_d\eta_{bc})=0$; thus the equation is $dU^a/d\tau=0$ in the inertial chart. Apply [F5] to each component on the interval to obtain constant $U=U_0$; applying it to $z^a(\tau)-U_0^a\tau$ gives $z(\tau)=X_0+(\tau-\tau_0)U_0$. Conversely a future-timelike proper-time straight curve has $dU/d\tau=0$ and is stationary by the reverse implication of [F3]. No compatible endpoint curve is asserted to exist for arbitrary endpoint events or arbitrary proper-time duration.

By [F4], $P=mU_0$ is constant, and [F2] gives $\pi_{A,1}=mU_1+qb x^1$. Differentiating along the curve from step 2.1 yields $d\pi_{A,1}/d\tau=qb U^1$, with $U_1=U^1$ by [F1]. Hence the canonical component may vary exactly as stated while $qF^\sharp(U)=0$ and $dP/d\tau=0$. The action shift has units joule-seconds and the canonical covector components have momentum units; neither is an empirical measurement.

boundaries.evidence: Statement requires tau0<tau1 and future-timelike C2 segments; no empty segment or zero tangent is admitted.
Step1.1 proves F=0 for every b; step3.1 records constant canonical component when q,b or U1 is zero.

boundaries.evidence: The massive model requires m,c>0 and timelike normalization; a null or zero-velocity spacetime tangent is excluded. Zero spatial U1 remains an allowed canonical-shift degeneracy.
Fixed events X0,X1 make the gauge action difference constant; step2.1 claims no solution for incompatible arbitrary endpoint/time data.
Inherited AComega is stated in Example,A2 and the action-equivalence proof use. No fullAC or extra choice construction is used.
Step2.1 uses the exact action equivalence, F=0 and constant flat metric to obtain constant U and straight motion.
Step2.1 states and proves the reverse implication: an admitted future-timelike proper-time straight curve has zero covariant acceleration and is stationary.
